checks.label: If you know the width and height of a rectangle, you can split it into squares and count them, to figure out its area: every floor drawn on a grid is split into its unit squares, and their count is width × height (4 m by 3 m is 12, the plant room 24, floors A and B 12 and 16, and every floor the corner can be dragged to, 1 by 1 up to 8 by 5)

The area of the triangle is half the area of the rectangle: a half-turn about its middle carries one half of the 6 m by 4 m rectangle exactly onto the other, each covering 12 of its 24 m²; the bracket plate's turned copy fills the rest of its 40 cm by 30 cm rectangle, 600 of 1,200 cm²

The base and the perpendicular height are at right angles to each other: each height is drawn straight up from a level base; for the top corner anywhere from 0 to 6 m along, the two outside pieces turned a half-turn land exactly on the triangle, so it covers 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 m²; the 6 cm triangle uses its 4 cm height, 12 cm², and its 5 cm sloping sides give 15 cm², which is wrong

Perimeter and area, worked from their rules: the plant room is 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 m around and covers 24 m²; floors A and B are both 16 m around but cover 12 m² and 16 m²; the L-shaped floors cover 12 + 6 = 20 − 2 = 18 m² and 20 + 4 = 30 − 6 = 24 m², and the second is 22 m around, the same as the 6 m by 5 m rectangle around it
Each puzzle's answer is worked out from its rule: 24 m²; floor B; a floor 4 m by 3 m (or 3 m by 4 m); 600 cm²; 12 cm²; 24 m²; 22 m

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and each wrong answer it names is the one a slip gives: all four sides added, two sides added, the same perimeter taken as the same area, the longer floor, a 3 m square 12 m around, a 12 m² floor with no 3 m side, the sloping side as the height, the whole rectangle, the whole rectangle around the room, the left part alone, only the labelled sides, the area's number; each is shown in the warning colour

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: no tint or running totals on the plant room, no areas on floors A and B, the drawn floor's area shown as ?, no rectangle, turned copy or sum on the triangles, no split or areas on the L-shaped room, the two unlabelled sides unlabelled, nothing in the warning colour

Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture, clear of each other and of the edges drawn, for every answer, right or wrong, wherever the floor's corner is dragged and wherever the top corner slides

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, and the turn after the top corner is let go, within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart
